title: Repackage SKUs into Usage Bundles and GTM Launch Orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Replace the current per-feature SKU model with 3 usage-oriented bundles (Starter, Scale, Enterprise) plus optional add-ons for dedicated capacity and private deployments. This ticket coordinates cross-functional deliverables needed for launch: SKU definitions, console UI labels, billing/quote path changes, migration tooling, release notes, support runbook, and sales enablement assets.

Scope:
- Finalize SKU table (limits, included tokens/embeddings, burst quotas, overage rules).
- Billing engine mapping and migration scripts for existing customers.
- Console UX: new plan picker, limits display, and upgrade modal copy.
- Docs & release notes: migration FAQ, changelog entry, API contract stability note.
- Sales & Support: enablement deck, migration playbook, pricing FAQ for negotiations.
- Telemetry: update billing metrics, usage dashboards, and revenue forecasting hooks.

Out of scope: billing tax treatment changes, long-term enterprise contract negotiation process (handled by Sales separately).

Acceptance criteria:
1) SKU table approved by Finance, Legal and Product.
2) Billing mapping PRs merged and stage-tested with 2 pilot customers.
3) Console UI shipped behind a feature flag and QA-signed.
4) Release notes drafted and sign-off from Comms and Support.
5) Sales enablement materials (deck + one-pager) completed and distributed to AEs.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pricing/2026-bundles (spec + migration rules)
- GitHub billing mapping PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/429
- Console branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/compare/feature/sku-bundles
- Pilot customer spreadsheet (internal Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pricing-pilot
- Launch dashboard (Looker): https://looker.redwood.ai/dashboards/pricing-migration

Rollout plan summary:
- Week -3 (Mar 10–16): Freeze SKU definitions; create release notes draft; begin pilot with 2 enterprise customers.
- Week -2 (Mar 17–23): Merge billing mapping, run migration dry-runs, feature-flag console UI to staging; prepare support playbook.
- Week -1 (Mar 24–30): Final QA, legal sign-off, sales enablement webinar, schedule announcement.
- Launch day (Mar 31): Promote feature flag to prod for new signups; run automated migration jobs during maintenance window; publish release notes and customer emails.
- Post-launch (Apr 1–14): Monitor telemetry, handle escalations, enable rollback path if critical billing regressions appear.

Rollback plan: revert console feature flag, pause migration jobs, re-run signed billing mapping fixes, notify affected customers and Sales.
